title: Tracking SDG 7: The Energy Progress Report 2024
authors: IEA, IRENA, UNSD, World Bank, WHO
description: The custodian agencies' annual assessment of global progress toward universal access to affordable, reliable, sustainable energy.

title: World Energy Outlook 2023
description: The IEA's flagship scenario analysis of the global energy system and the pace of the clean-energy transition.

title: World Energy Transitions Outlook 2023
description: IRENA's 1.5°C pathway detailing the renewables scale-up, electrification, and investment needed to meet climate goals.

title: Energy Access and the Sustainable Development Goals
description: ESMAP research on closing the energy-access gap for the 675 million people still living without electricity.

title: The Geopolitics of the Energy Transition
description: 'A New World'—examines how the shift to renewables reshapes global power, trade, and security.

title: Just Transition of the Workforce
description: The ILO Guidelines for a just transition toward environmentally sustainable economies and societies for all.

title: Scaling Up Renewable Energy in Developing Countries
description: Analysis of the finance, policy, and grid reforms needed to accelerate renewables deployment in the Global South.

title: Cooking with Clean Energy: Access and Health
description: WHO evidence on the 2.3 billion people relying on polluting cooking fuels and the resulting health burden.

title: The Role of Critical Minerals in Clean Energy Transitions
description: The IEA's assessment of mineral demand, supply risks, and the sustainability challenges of the energy transition.

title: Solar Power and Rural Electrification in South Asia
description: Reviews decentralised solar and off-grid electrification models expanding energy access in rural South Asia.

title: Energy Subsidy Reform: Lessons and Implications
description: The IMF's influential analysis of the fiscal, environmental, and distributional case for reforming fossil-fuel subsidies.

title: Powering Jobs: The Employment Footprint of Renewable Energy
description: The annual review estimating renewable-energy employment worldwide and its distribution across technologies and regions.

title: Improving Energy Access, Climate and Socio-Economic Outcomes Through Off-Grid Electrification Technologies: A Systematic Review
description: 47 impact evaluations of off-grid solar, from 18 databases and 29 grey sources. Kerosene use falls and uptake rises; reliability, affordability and energy expenditure do not move, and the effect on time spent studying shows publication bias. The most honest evidence map in this field.
journal: Campbell Systematic Reviews: Better Evidence for a Better World

title: The false optimism of electrification: why universal electricity access has not delivered urban energy transformation in South Africa
description: Argues that counting grid connections measures proximity to a wire, not access to energy services, and that households in un-serviceable settlements are permanently excluded by design. Directly relevant to anyone reading SDG 7 progress figures.

title: Distributional justice and rapid green energy transitions: citizen experiences in Kenya
description: Kenya is on track for SDG 7 and is held up as the African success case. Focus groups and survey data show the poor carrying the cost of the transition, and a gap between the national narrative and what citizens report.

title: Beyond access: clean energy use in low-income and middle-income countries
description: Makes the measurement argument plainly: SDG 7's binary indicators overstate health and equity gains because they cannot see fuel stacking, dynamic consumption or the gendered burden of polluting fuels.

title: An Ecohealth approach to energy justice: Evidence from Malawi’s energy transition from biomass to electrification
description: Malawi runs biomass cooking and hydroelectricity at once, so deforestation silts the rivers that generate the power. An argument for analysing energy systems against both human health and ecosystem function rather than one at a time.

title: Energy justice and gender: bridging equity, access, and policy for sustainable development
description: 616 publications mapped against SDG 5 and SDG 7. Finds clean energy adoption reduces unpaid domestic work and strengthens women's economic opportunities, and that policies written without a gender lens tend to entrench the inequalities they meant to relieve.
